messages.subject: Compilation Error PyStan
parts:
Hi all,


I'm having trouble running a script I got from a colleague on my mac. We have the same set up, i.e. pyStan 2.12.0 with Anaconda python 2.7, the same installation with pip,  I've just updated Xcode, and numpy and cython requirements are being met. 


import pystan
import numpy as np
import scipy
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
%matplotlib inline
print np.version.version
print(pystan.__version__)
import cython
print(cython.__version__)

1.11.2
2.12.0.0
0.24.1

model = """
data {
  int N; // number of bins
  vector[N] x; // bin midpoints
  vector[N] dx; // bin widths
  int counts[N]; // binned Poisson counts
}

transformed data {
  matrix[N,N] sq_dist; // matrix of pairwise squared distances

  for (j in 1:N) {
    for (k in 1:N) {
      sq_dist[j,k] = (x[k] - x[j]) ^ 2;
    }
  }   
}

parameters {
  real<lower=0> lengthscale;
  real beta;           // linear slope  
  real<lower=0> sigma; // log standard deviation
  real mu;             // GP mean (here a constant function)
  vector[N] latents;   // latent GP values
}

model {
  matrix[N, N] Cov; // covariance matrix for the GP
  // squared exponential covariance plus linear covariance, with fudge factor 0.001 added to diagonal
  Cov = sigma^2 * exp(- sq_dist / lengthscale^2) + beta^2 * x * (x') + diag_matrix(rep_vector(0.001, N)); 

  // likelihood of observered counts -- note that we are modeling the log rate with the latent GP.
  // isn't this a postierior? how are counts passed in?
  counts ~ poisson_log(latents + mu + log(dx));

  // priors -- note flat prior on beta
  latents ~ multi_normal(rep_vector(0, N), Cov);
  lengthscale ~ lognormal(0, 5);
  sigma ~ lognormal(0, 5);
}

generated quantities {  
  vector[N] rates;
  // Poisson rates
  rates = exp(latents + mu) .* dx;
}
"""

dat = { 'N': N, 'x': xvalO, 'dx': dx, 'counts': yvalO.astype(int) }

fit = pystan.stan(model_code=model, data=dat, iter=1000, chains=1, verbose = True)

On Wednesday, October 19, 2016 at 12:28:00 AM UTC-4, Meghan Frate wrote:
I'm having trouble running a script I got from a colleague on my mac. We have the same set up, i.e. pyStan 2.12.0 with Anaconda python 2.7, the same installation with pip,  I've just updated Xcode, and numpy and cython requirements are being met.

This seems to be using
GCC 4.2.1

 I don't think we support that compiler anymore. You need to try to compile things with clang++.

Ben
